context.body: Gad came that day to David and said to him, “Go up, build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”.

observations.body: Gad directs an altar; Araunah offers place, animals, and wood, but David insists on purchase, pays fifty silver shekels for floor and oxen, sacrifices, and the plague is stopped.
observations.label: David buys the threshing floor and builds an altar: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Gad, David, Araunah, the LORD, and Israel, Araunah’s threshing floor in Jerusalem, ascending, bowing, offering, refusing a costless gift, buying, building, sacrificing, and answering prayer visible within David's story or later memory.

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 24:18–25 as its own famine, song, last words, and census David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places purchased ground, altar, offering, and stopped plague converge inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
